subject: tech
title: On and Off: Computer Codes
about: Deep inside, a computer keeps everything with tiny switches that are only on or off, written as 1 and 0: a row of lights spells a code, a yes-or-no answer is one bit, numbers can spell a word, three numbers can mix a color, and a little picture like an envelope stands for an idea (K2-AP-02, K2-NI-01). Binary is a bridge topic, taught from Grade 3 on, so the cards stay with lights, codes and colors he can see and count. Read it together with a flashlight in hand: on, off, on.
tip: Use a flashlight to send on, off, on across the room, then let him send a code back and tell you its 1s and 0s.

cards.q: Inside a computer, words, pictures and songs are all kept as which two numbers?
cards.note: Everything in a computer is long rows of 1s and 0s. 1 is on, 0 is off.

cards.q: Writing everything with only 1 and 0 has a grown-up name. What is it?
cards.note: Binary means made of two, and you say it BY-nah-ree. You will learn more about it in a few years.

cards.q: A computer is full of tiny switches. Each switch can be only two ways. Which two?
cards.note: On is 1 and off is 0. Millions of tiny switches make everything the computer does.

cards.q: 💡 ⚫ 💡 The lights are on, off, on. 1 means on. Which code is it?
cards.sayQ: Three lights: on, off, on. One means on and zero means off. Which code is it?
cards.note: Read the lights left to right: on is 1, off is 0. One, zero, one.

cards.q: The code is 0 1 1 and 1 means on. Which lights are on?
cards.sayQ: The code is zero, one, one, and one means on. Which lights are on?
cards.note: Zero is off, so the first light is dark. The two 1s at the end are on.

cards.q: A yes-or-no answer fits in a single 1 or 0. That tiny piece has a name. What is it?
cards.sayQ: A yes-or-no answer fits in a single one or zero. That tiny piece has a name. What is it?
cards.note: A bit is the smallest piece of computer data: one 1 or one 0, one yes or one no.

cards.q: One light can be on or off. How many different things can it show?
cards.note: On means one thing, off means another. One light, two choices.

cards.q: Two lights can be on on, on off, off on, or off off. How many different codes is that?
cards.sayQ: Two lights can be: on and on, on and off, off and on, or off and off. How many different codes is that?
cards.note: Count them: on on, on off, off on, off off. Two lights make four codes.

cards.q: Three friends each want their own light code. One light makes only 2 codes. How many lights do you need?
cards.note: Two lights make 4 codes, and 3 friends need only 3. One light makes just 2, so it is one short.

cards.q: A is 1, B is 2, C is 3, D is 4. Which word do the numbers 3 1 2 spell?
cards.sayQ: The letter A is one, B is two, C is three, D is four. Which word do the numbers three, one, two spell?
cards.note: 3 is C, 1 is A, 2 is B. Numbers can spell words: that is how a computer keeps them.

cards.q: A is 1, B is 2, C is 3, D is 4. Which word do the numbers 4 1 4 spell?
cards.sayQ: The letter A is one, B is two, C is three, D is four. Which word do the numbers four, one, four spell?
cards.note: 4 is D, 1 is A, 4 is D again. Dad!

cards.q: A is 1, B is 2, C is 3, D is 4. Which numbers spell the word bad?
cards.sayQ: The letter A is one, B is two, C is three, D is four. Which numbers spell the word bad?
cards.note: B is 2, A is 1, D is 4. Now you can write a secret number message.

cards.q: A screen dot mixes red, green and blue light. Its numbers are red 9, green 0, blue 0. What color is it?
cards.note: Only the red light is on, so the dot looks red. Three numbers make every color.

cards.q: A dot's red number tells how much red light it makes. Which is brighter, red 2 or red 9?
cards.note: Bigger number, brighter light. Zero means that light is off.

cards.q: A dot's numbers are red 0, green 0, blue 0. All three lights are off. What color is the dot?
cards.note: No light at all looks black. Turn all three lights up high and the dot looks white.

cards.q: A row of a picture is 1 1 1 0. Here 1 means a black square. How many black squares?
cards.sayQ: A row of a picture is one, one, one, zero. Here one means a black square. How many black squares?
cards.note: Count the 1s: three black squares and one white one. Every pixel is a number.

cards.q: A row of a picture is 0 0 1 0. Here 1 means black. Which square is black?
cards.sayQ: A row of a picture is zero, zero, one, zero. Here one means black. Which square is black?
cards.note: Read left to right: white, white, black, white. The 1 sits in the third spot.

cards.q: A tiny envelope picture on the screen is a symbol. What does it stand for?
cards.note: A symbol stands for something else. An envelope means message, a red light means stop, and 1 means on.
